promises.label: Launch $30,000 Universal EVs
promises.commitment: Launch the Universal EV Platform in 2027, underpinning products starting around $30,000.
promises.outcomeSummary: Universal EV launch remained pending for 2027. Fathom was on track for fourth quarter next year, with a $28,350 starting MSRP.

missing.what_was_said: Andrew Frick said Ford was “right on track to share our plans with dealers and take customer orders later this year,” meaning 2026. This earlier order-taking milestone is absent from the chronology; S7 subsequently gives early 2027 for preorders.

Kumar Galhotra reported that 90% of validation testing was complete and Ford had built its first production-line vehicles at Louisville. The principal remaining launch risk was ensuring suppliers could run at rate with high-quality parts. These were preparation milestones, not a completed customer launch.

promises.label: Cut 2026 industrial costs
promises.commitment: Deliver another $1 billion of industrial cost improvements in 2026, redeploying savings into accretive ICE and hybrid product plans.
promises.outcomeSummary: Ford remained on track for $1 billion of material and warranty cost reductions, excluding Novelis and tariffs; savings were to fund UEV and Ford Energy. Completion remained pending.

promises.label: Reach 8% company EBIT margin
promises.commitment: Achieve an 8% company adjusted EBIT margin by 2029.
promises.outcomeSummary: Ford continued to target an 8% company adjusted EBIT margin by 2029; management reaffirmed the goal, which remained pending.

missing.what_was_said: Jim Farley said profitability in 2027 was expected to be roughly in line with 2026 and called 2027 a “foundational year on our journey to 8%.” This qualified the near-term pace of improvement without changing the 2029 target.

promises.label: Bring Model e to breakeven
promises.commitment: Bring Ford Model e to breakeven in 2029.
promises.outcomeSummary: Model e remained loss-making. Ford retained breakeven by 2029 while warning of higher expenses in 2027 and nonlinear progress.

missing.what_was_said: Asked whether improvement toward breakeven would be back-end-loaded, CFO Sherry House said investors could expect steady improvement throughout the period, supported by UEV products arriving in 2027 and becoming more profitable in 2028 and beyond.

While retaining the 2029 breakeven target, House said progress would not be linear and expenses were now expected to be higher in 2027. The next step-function improvement in profitability was expected in the first half of 2028 as UEV and Ford Energy ramped revenue.

promises.label: Build Ford Energy battery capacity
promises.commitment: Establish 20 gigawatt hours of Ford Energy capacity in 2027 and beyond.
promises.outcomeSummary: Still pending: Ford reaffirmed at least 20 GWh annually, with first customer deliveries planned for late 2027.

missing.what_was_said: Dave Carroll said the team was focused on launching the initial 20 GWh and bringing it online and ramping up in 2028. This adds production-ramp context to the separately reaffirmed end-2027 capacity milestone.

Management reported that Kentucky had met every operating milestone so far and completed electrode-mixing trial runs. Executed contracts plus late-stage negotiations covered more than 80% of Ford Energy's 2028 capacity, with full commitment expected by Q1 2027.
